The function does not decide from fs.existsSync alone: it ANDs four fs.existsSync checks with a hasCompleteWebArtifacts call (252-272) that parses index.html, resolves every src/href reference under the public root, and statSyncs each one — a stronger check than bare existence. Fixed in four places: (1) Rationale now describes the real check and isolates the missing property to freshness; (2) the Requirement body now says the freshness comparison is ADDED to the existence/completeness check rather than replacing it, closing a real implementation hazard where a fix might have swapped out the completeness check; (3) AC-1 names hasDeploymentArtifacts/hasCompleteWebArtifacts as checks that must be retained; (4) the Trace Link note describes both functions with real line ranges. scope_decision.rationale: Option (a) — widen OPS-BGSTAB-003 to all ten pane-* RED tests — was chosen over (b) creating a separate requirement for pane-split/pane-persistence. Reasons, in order of weight. (1) Single root cause: all seven newly covered tests fail for exactly the same reason as TC-6602, which OPS-BGSTAB-003 already owns — .pane-leaf has zero occurrences in frontend/src and exists only in helpers.ts and the pane-* specs. Splitting one cause across two requirements would put the same responsibility in two places, the failure mode where one side gets fixed and the other silently diverges. (2) The requirement's existing structure already absorbs the widening at zero structural cost: it was built around per-test dispositions (A/B/C) with explicitly different causes per test, so adding seven tests with a shared cause needed enumeration and a cause-2 grouping, not a new mechanism. (3) The pre-existing Implementation Note already acknowledged that pane-split.spec.ts and pane-persistence.spec.ts use the same .pane-leaf selector, and then declared them out of scope — the requirement had already identified the seven tests and chosen not to disposition them. Widening resolves that acknowledged gap in place; option (b) would have preserved it as a cross-requirement seam. (4) Single dependency edge: OPS-BGSTAB-005 AC-7 is judged from one piece of evidence (OPS-BGSTAB-003 AC-2). Option (b) would have made AC-7 depend on two requirements' evidence, and a partial-evidence state (one closed, one open) would make AC-7 undecidable again — reintroducing the exact defect being fixed. (5) Cost of (b) was strictly higher: a new draft requirement adds an SRS-W023 warning and a second Change-Note lineage for a proposition that is textually near-identical to AC-5. No countervailing reason to split was found: the two spec files share the cause, the disposition menu, the verification command, and the single downstream consumer. AC-1 still permits per-test disposition choices, so the widening does not force the seven tests into a single all-or-nothing outcome.
